data.claim: Overriding Popen._try_wait to call os.wait4 yields the child's own cpu, maxrss and block io; a 150 MB allocating child is reported >=140 MB and a following trivial child reports its own small numbers.
data.falsifier: A trivial command after the heavy one reporting the heavy one's maxrss, or metered reap costing more than 5 ms over a plain Popen.
data.mechanism: wait4 returns the rusage of exactly the reaped pid (and its waited descendants); RUSAGE_CHILDREN is a cumulative process-wide total with maxrss a high-water mark, so only wait4 is per-command.
data.probe_output: 12 passed (real child: maxrss>=140MB, cpu>=0.35s; follow-up true: maxrss<50MB; overhead <5ms)
data.question: Does a Popen subclass reaping via os.wait4 give each shell line its own rusage at negligible overhead?
